text:
alex.m: POC with RemitCorp is blocked — streaming responses from our Python SDK hang when their users are behind the corporate proxy. No exception, client just stalls after first chunk.
paul-sales: They are an enterprise deal (security questionnaire in flight). They want to validate streaming latencies before committing to Dedicated. Any quick fixes?
devon.eng: Which SDK version and transport? websocket or HTTP streaming? Also can you paste the client-side logs and a server request id if available?
alex.m: Using python-sdk v0.9.2, HTTP streaming (stream=True). Here's the client log around the hang:
```
2026-03-19 14:12:02 INFO request: POST /v1/generate 200 OK
2026-03-19 14:12:02 INFO response: received 1 chunk
2026-03-19 14:12:32 WARNING socket: read timeout after 30s
# no error propagated to app, process is waiting on stream iterator
```
paul-sales: They run Zscaler and an F5 proxy in path. Also asked about Dedicated pricing — I told them we'd share a draft contract once we unblock the POC.
devon.eng: Common with proxies that do TLS inspection — they either terminate CONNECT or mutate chunked frames. Two immediate checks: 1) try curl through their proxy with --no-keepalive to reproduce, 2) check whether proxy returns 200 for CONNECT then injects data. Can you grab a packet trace or proxy logs?
lina-sre: Also confirm environment variables (HTTPS_PROXY/HTTP_PROXY/NO_PROXY) and whether the proxy requires NTLM/Negotiate auth. NTLM often breaks streaming because of repeated handshake bytes.
alex.m: They use delegated auth (NTLM). I tried setting HTTPS_PROXY but got a 502 from the proxy after ~20s. curl output: 
```
* Connected to proxy.company.com (10.0.0.1) port 8080
> CONNECT inference.redwood.ai:443 HTTP/1.1
< HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
< Content-Length: 0
```
devon.eng: If NTLM in the middle, requests library may not forward upstream chunked frames properly. Two options:
- Use requests-ntlm for auth + stream, or
- Bypass proxy for our endpoints (NO_PROXY for inference.redwood.ai) if company policy allows.
Try this Python snippet to force smaller read timeouts and keepalive: 
```python
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=..., timeout=(10,60), stream=True)  # connect/read timeouts
for chunk in client.generate(...):
    if not chunk: break
    print(chunk)
```
devon.eng: Also can you try websocket transport? Websockets often survive enterprise proxies better if they allow CONNECT and keep TLS intact. We have websocket toggle in the SDK: transport="ws".
sam.ops: Quick note — if their proxy is doing TLS interception, we might have to provide them with our cert pinning docs or suggest a bypass for this host in their proxy policy. Security team likes signed cert bundles for Dedicated.
alex.m: Tried websocket -> client fails at TLS handshake: "SSL: WRONG_VERSION_NUMBER". Looks like proxy is doing active TLS interception and re-negotiation.
lina-sre: For NTLM specifically, ask them to enable tunnel mode for inference.redwood.ai (no inspection). If they can't, request a proxy config that preserves chunked transfer and keeps connection alive. I can draft a one-pager for their infra team.
devon.eng: Another workaround: switch SDK to short-polling (non-streaming) for the POC to validate correctness. Not ideal for latency but useful to unblock. Use generate(..., stream=False) and poll until complete.
alex.m: Short-polling works for correctness tests, but customer cares about perceived latency — they want streaming.
paul-sales: From deal perspective, if RemitCorp can prove streaming works with a minimal proxy exception, legal/security will greenlight Dedicated. We need an ask to their infra: a proxy bypass for inference.redwood.ai or a proxy rule to allow raw TLS CONNECT. I'll send that as a checklist.
devon.eng: I'll reproduce with a local NTLM/Zscaler-like appliance this afternoon. If I can replicate, we can craft an SDK patch that better surfaces read timeouts and adds a fallback to short-polling automatically.
deploy-bot: Canary deploy of proxy-handling tweak finished to canary infra at 14:30 :white_check_mark:
alex.m: Thanks — please share the one-pager for their infra and a short-term SDK flag we can flip. I'll push the checklist to RemitCorp infra and loop them in.
sam.ops: I'll prep the SOC2/attestation snippets for their security questionnaire and draft a Dedicated pricing note to include with the workaround plan.
paul-sales: Great — plan: 1) alex sends proxy logs + curl trace to eng, 2) devon reproduces, 3) eng provides one-pager + short-term SDK fallback, 4) sales sends pricing + security docs. Keep me posted. :thumbsup:
